clue.text: Measure of an Arab's capacity for work?

definitions.text: Measure of an Arab's capacity for work?

parts.words: Measure of an Arab's capacity for work?
parts.note: an Arab is a breed of horse, so the working capacity of such an animal is the unit engineers use for engine power

explanation.surface: Someone wonders how to gauge how hard a person from Arabia can work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arab' looks like a person, but here it is the horse breed, and the unit of power is literally named for a horse's work.
explanation.definitionFit: The unit of engine output was originally defined by the work rate of a draught animal.

clue.text: Aerial I had set up on post

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the letters are raised, read from bottom to top

parts.note: I had contracts to I'd, giving ID
a post is an upright pole

explanation.surface: An antenna that I had mounted on a post.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'set up' reverses upward; 'on' means placed after, as the post supports the aerial.
explanation.definitionFit: A dipole is a simple type of radio antenna, which the British call an aerial.

clue.text: Old women left deranged, upset, with stingers around

indicators.note: the stinging insects are placed around the other letters, enclosing them

parts.note: bees are insects that sting

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: deranged means mad

explanation.surface: Elderly women gone mad, upset, with bees swarming about them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reverses the word for deranged; 'Old women' is the definition, an archaic term.
explanation.definitionFit: A beldam is an archaic word for an old woman, often a hag-like one.

clue.text: Deficient Conservative in panic

indicators.note: the abbreviation sits inside the word for panic

parts.note: a scare is a sudden panic
C is the abbreviation for Conservative, the British party

explanation.surface: A lacking Conservative politician caught in a panic.
explanation.definitionFit: Something scarce is in short supply, that is deficient in quantity.

clue.text: Lock up mischief-maker, revolutionary Irish boy

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous little devil or child

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the abbreviation is reversed

parts.note: a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A call to jail a troublemaker, a rebellious Irish lad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' here means turning round, not a political rebel.
explanation.definitionFit: To imprison someone is to lock them up in jail.

clue.text: Servant's contribution to book?

definitions.meaning: a young male attendant in a household or hotel
one leaf of a book, one side of which is a printed sheet

explanation.surface: A servant's share in writing a book.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A page is both a boy attendant and a single sheet side in a book.

clue.text: View of professional put on record

parts.note: pro is short for professional
a file is a record kept on something

explanation.surface: An expert's opinion is put on the record.
explanation.definitionFit: A profile is a side view, especially of a face or an outline.

clue.text: Soldier to brood with one cold fellow-soldier as a hanger-on

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper
a hen sits on eggs to brood them
I is the Roman numeral one
C stands for cold, as on taps
an ally fights on the same side

explanation.surface: A soldier hatches eggs alongside a chilly comrade, living off others.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting parasitically means living off another, as a sponger or hanger-on does.

clue.text: Order fellow to be brought into company doctor

indicators.note: the fellow is placed inside the letters for doctor

parts.note: MD is a Doctor of Medicine
a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: An instruction for a man to be taken to the firm's doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A command is an order given with authority.

clue.text: Loose women said to mingle with monied men

indicators.note: mingling mixes the letters of the words together into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Women of easy virtue are reputed to socialise with rich men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' looks like a homophone signal but is fodder: SAID and MONIEDMEN rearranged give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The French term for women of the fringe of respectable society, kept by wealthy lovers.

clue.text: Think after short break provides one with the answer

indicators.note: the word for think comes after the shortened break
short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a rest is a break
to ponder is to think

explanation.surface: After a brief pause for thought, someone comes up with the answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' removes a final letter; 'provides' is only a link between wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A responder is someone who replies, giving a reply or answer.

clue.text: Watery fluid the man's put into alcoholic drink

indicators.note: the pronoun is placed inside the drink

parts.note: rum is a spirit
the man is he; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: Something watery the fellow has added to his tipple.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheum is a thin discharge from the eyes or nose.

clue.text: Austrian composer makes little girl keep very quiet

indicators.note: keeping means holding the music mark inside the name

parts.note: Sue is a short girl's name, from Susan
pp, pianissimo, is the musical mark for very quiet

explanation.surface: A young girl is told to stay hushed for a composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz von Suppe was a 19th-century composer of Viennese operettas.

clue.text: Eddy gets left in some tram that's broken down

indicators.note: the abbreviation goes inside the rearranged letters
a broken-down vehicle's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man called Eddy is stranded on a tram that has broken down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eddy' looks like a name, but is a whirlpool. SOMETRAM rearranged gives MAESTROM, with L inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A maelstrom is a powerful whirlpool, a violent swirling current.

clue.text: Back with soldiers in dull initiative to prepare for war again?

definitions.text: initiative to prepare for war again?

parts.note: the rear is the back

indicators.note: the soldiers sit inside the word for dull

parts.note: matt means dull, without shine; here spelt mat
men are soldiers, as in officers and men

explanation.surface: Soldiers return to a lacklustre plan to make ready for conflict once more.
explanation.definitionFit: Rearmament is the process of equipping forces with weapons again.

clue.text: Regarding message on hospital sign?

definitions.meaning: a hospital signpost would point the way to the wards

explanation.surface: Wondering about what a hospital sign says.
explanation.definitionFit: The preposition means concerning or with regard to, and split it reads to the wards.

clue.text: Sort of cat trailing around

indicators.note: around here means scattered about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cat trails about.
explanation.definitionFit: The ringtail is a raccoon-like animal of North America, sometimes called a ringtail cat.

clue.text: Not in favour of having article in vessel's hold

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons

indicators.note: the article goes inside the container

parts.note: a tin is a vessel; the possessive is ignored
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Opposed to keeping an item in a ship's hold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hold' looks like a ship's cargo space, but it is a verb meaning to hold within.
explanation.definitionFit: To contain something is to hold it within.

clue.text: Fruit that may be dear in France starts to ripen in early summer

parts.note: cher is French for dear

indicators.note: the first letters of each of the following words are taken

explanation.surface: Fruit that may be expensive in France begins ripening early in summer.
explanation.definitionFit: Cherries are small stone fruits that ripen early in summer.

clue.text: Story lasting a long time — false story I avoided

parts.note: chronic describes something persisting for a long time

indicators.note: avoided means the letter is left out of the word

parts.note: a lie is a false story

explanation.surface: A tale that drags on: a false story I steered clear of.
explanation.definitionFit: A chronicle is a historical account, a story of events.

clue.text: Bird we hear make a puffing sound

indicators.note: we hear means the word sounds like another when said

parts.note: a steam engine chuffs, making a puffing noise

explanation.surface: A bird that sounds like it is panting.
explanation.walkthrough: Many readers say the bird's name to rhyme with 'tough'.
explanation.definitionFit: The chough is a red-billed member of the crow family found on coastal cliffs.

clue.text: Butterfly that may make someone speaking pause

definitions.meaning: an orange butterfly with ragged wings and a white mark

definitions.text: that may make someone speaking pause
definitions.meaning: a punctuation mark tells a reader aloud to pause briefly

explanation.surface: A butterfly might make a speaker stop mid-sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: The punctuation mark marks a short pause, and it also names a ragged-winged butterfly.

clue.text: Theatrical fellow who would shy away from difficulties?

definitions.meaning: Noel ..., the English playwright and actor

definitions.text: who would shy away from difficulties?
definitions.meaning: someone lacking courage who avoids hard things

explanation.surface: An actor who avoids trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Noel Coward was a celebrated English dramatist, and the common noun means a timid person.

clue.text: Frontier this writer's established in literature

indicators.note: the setter's phrase is placed inside the abbreviation

parts.note: this writer is the setter, me; this writer's is I'm

explanation.surface: The writer has settled into the edge of literature.
explanation.definitionFit: A limit is a boundary or border, a frontier.

clue.text: Cut makes one grumble audibly

indicators.note: audibly means the word is said, matching another

parts.note: to moan is to grumble

explanation.surface: A trim makes someone complain out loud.
explanation.definitionFit: Mown is the past participle of mow, said of grass that has been cut.

clue.text: Females getting into row

parts.note: row means to pull oars, not a quarrel, so these women are taking up rowing

explanation.surface: Women about to start an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' wants to be a quarrel; it is rowing a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Women who row boats are rowers, the female members of a crew.

clue.text: Shelter at back of yard, showing sign of tiredness?

indicators.note: the last letter of the word is taken

parts.note: an awning is a canvas shelter

explanation.surface: A canopy at the far end of the garden, looking weary.
explanation.definitionFit: Yawning, opening the mouth wide, is a typical sign of being tired.

clue.text: Go wrong and start to spoil jobs

parts.note: to err is to go wrong
taken as written

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Things go wrong and start to spoil the chores.
explanation.definitionFit: Errands are short trips or tasks done for someone, small jobs.
